I've been thinking about this for a while now, and I just don't think it can be saved. I don't think there's any possible way to prevent it's abuse. No matter what, so long as the downvoat button exists, shallow, reactionary cowards will click it just because they disagree with something. And that's the least of the problems. As more ex-Redditors have moved over here, brigading has already taken hold, and it's only going to get worse. Something needs to be done, and I'm thinking more and more that that's eliminating the function entirely.

With only an upvote button, good threads will still rise to the top anyway, so that's fine. The only potential problem is bad threads, but I don't think it would really be a problem.

Bluntly, downvoting already has little real impact, because many mods don't even allow it to do its job. The idea is supposed to be that bad threads sink out of sight as they're downvoted, but the reality on many subs (and virtually all of the high profile ones) is that overzealous mods are deleting any problem threads (and potentially even non-problem threads) before downvoting can even make a difference. So it's already largely not serving its intended purpose and won't be missed as far as that goes anyway.

And on a narrower scale - just a ranking of the popularity of threads without the additional notion of "punishing" bad ones - upvotes are the only thing that matter anyway. Threads without upvotes will sink anyway, and that's sufficient.

I'm not 100% convinced that this is the answer, but it's the one I keep coming back to.
I'm beginning to think that downvoting should be eliminated entirely.

Why keep upvoting if you want to do away with downvoting?

Rank posts based on the amount of conversation using an equation that factors in: number of unique accounts engaged in the conversation, average length of reply, number of unique words/sentences, number of replies, average length of comment threads, frequency of replies, time since last reply.
